draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Malabar Hill! It's one of Mumbai's most affluent neighbourhoods, and it all began when Governor Mountstuart Elphinstone built the first bungalow up here between 1819 and 1827.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat in my notes for Malabar Hill, so wander down towards Kemps Corner and see what tempts you.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Hanging Gardens are just a 4 minute walk, Kamala Nehru Park is 6 minutes, and the old Babulnath Temple is about 9 minutes away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a bench in the Hanging Gardens for the sunset over the Arabian Sea, or look down at the Queen's Necklace from Kamala Nehru Park.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Seen from the air, the walkway inside the Hanging Gardens spells out PMG, for Pherozeshah Mehta Gardens, in cursive.

spots.name: Hanging Gardens of Mumbai
spots.detail: 4 min walk · Terraced gardens with hedges clipped into animal shapes

spots.name: Kamala Nehru Park
spots.detail: 6 min walk · The Old Woman's Shoe and views of Marine Drive below

spots.name: Mani Bhavan
spots.detail: 14 min walk · Gandhi's Mumbai base from 1917 to 1934, now a museum

legends.title: A lid on the reservoir
legends.body: The gardens were laid out over Bombay's main reservoir. Some say it was done to shield the water from the nearby Towers of Silence.

tips.title: Time it for sunset.
tips.body: The Hanging Gardens face west, so evening gives you the best views over the Arabian Sea.

tips.title: See Jinnah House from outside.
tips.body: South Court, Jinnah's old home, is closed to the public because of property disputes.

story.title: Walkeshwar Temple
story.body: The Silhara kings founded the Walkeshwar Temple here. The Portuguese destroyed it, and Rama Kamath rebuilt it in 1715.

story.title: The first bungalow
story.body: Governor Mountstuart Elphinstone built the first bungalow on Malabar Hill. Others followed, and it soon became the wealthy area it still is.

story.title: Gardens and a church
story.body: The Hanging Gardens were laid out over the city's main reservoir. All Saints' Church was built the same year so locals didn't have to travel 8 km to Fort.

story.title: Freedom struggle next door
story.body: Gandhi worked from Mani Bhavan, and gave the Quit India speech at nearby Gowalia Tank on 8 August 1942. Jinnah lived at South Court until he left for Karachi in 1946.

story.title: Home of the powerful
story.body: The Chief Minister's Varsha Bungalow and the Sahyadri guest house are here. Business tycoons and film stars live on the hill too.
